According to Polybius, as Scipio watched Carthage burn he wept, and then:

After musing by himself a long time and reflecting upon the inevitable fall of cities, peoples and empires, as well as of individuals, upon the fate of Troy, that once proud city, upon the fate of the Assyrians, the Median, and afterwards of the great Persian empire, and most recently of all, of the splendid empire of Macedon, either voluntarily or otherwise the words of the poet [Homer] escape from his lips:

The day shall come in which our sacred Troy

And Priam, and the people over whom

Spear-bearing Priam rules, shall perish all.

Being asked by Polybius in casual conversation (for Polybius had been his tutor) what he meant by using these words, Polybius says that he did not hesitate to frankly name his own country, for whose fate he feared when he considered the mutability of human affairs. And Polybius wrote this down just as he heard it.

So I had a panic attack this week. For those that don't know I'm a T2 diabetic, yes, not all of us are fat.

I keep my sugars under control through a strict diet, exercise, and vigilant monitoring. I'm out to dinner this week with a supplier, benchmark my glucose at 83mg/dl before the meal... normal fasting. The dish I ordered was a pretty simple chicken dish with veggies and some sauce. I planned to have half of it, but I didn't like the way the sauce tasted/felt. One bite and I was pretty convinced it was loaded with sugar which is a panic trigger for me, so I called over the waiter and asked, he went back, came out and said, no the sauce didn't really have much sugar.

I should have made him bring out the chef, but I'm with a supplier, and I don't want to make a scene, so I divided the dish up, and change plans to only eat a third of it. My blood sugar goes up by about 1.5mg/dl per carb consumed, and I try and keep it <140mg/dl, so even if the dish had 115g of carbs (more than a starbeetus drink), I'll be ok with eating one third.

I finished maybe a quarter because I could just tell the sauce was loaded, and it was stressing me out, and tried to put it out of my mind. Meeting with the supplier went well, we're looking to source some new sensor PCBs, and I need a good supplier who can help me get the cost down. We're building a new device to help kids track their blood sugar and activity, and I want this to be coverable by medicare/medicaid so we can help kids in disadvantaged socioeconomic groups. Because government healthcare ought to help children, not pay for fats.

An hour after dinner my timer goes off, and I check my sugars, this is part of my routine, and part of being a responsible T2. I stab myself, draw some blood and read.

211mg/dl

I haven't been above 140 in over a year, I am very strict. But worse, I can use this number to calculate what was in the meal. See part of my T2 is I don't have an upper bookend on my blood sugar like you do. If you eat too many carbs, your body buffers it down, and keeps you safe. For me, I have to restrict intake to what I can handle and process. My response is roughly linear, with a 1.5mg/dl rise at 60-90m post meal per gram of accessible carbohydrate.

This means in the 1/4 of the dish I ate, there were 85 fucking grams of carbs. So the whole dish? 341g of carbs. 341!!! WHAT THE FUCK.
